name: Dimensional Analysis and Similarity
description: Introduction to dimensional analysis; history, motivation, drawbacks of brute force experimentation, drag coefficient example. Dimensional analysis using mathematical models: damped oscillations, transient conduction, viscous flows; importance of dimensionless numbers in fluid mechanics and heat transfer. Techniques: rules of thumb, Ipsen’s method, combining with intuition and experiments; Taylor’s atomic bomb estimate. Buckingham pi theorem: pressure drop in pipe, drag on bodies, surface roughness; comparison with Ipsen’s method. Model studies: geometric, kinematic, dynamic similarity; prototypes of submarines, boats. Riabouchinsky–Rayleigh paradox and rules of relevance. Self-similarity: first and second kind, Falkner–Skan, nonlinear diffusion. Intermediate asymptotics: blast waves, droplet spreading.
